bibl.title: Dating Ancient Egyptian Papyri through Raman Spectroscopy: Concept and Application to the Fragments of the Gospel of Jesus' Wife and the Gospel of John.
bibl.seg: Sarah Goler, James T. Yardley, David M. Ratzan, Roger Bagnall, Alexis Hagadorn & James McInerney, Dating Ancient Egyptian Papyri through Raman Spectroscopy: Concept and Application to the Fragments of the Gospel of Jesus' Wife and the Gospel of John.
Journal for the Study of the New Testament 42 (2019) pp. 98-133, figg.
bibl.note: Paper presented at an SBL panel (San Antonio, Texas, Nov. 21, 2016). - Introduction. - The Ancient Ink Laboratory. - Raman spectroscopy. - Carbon, chars and soots. - The AIL Raman experiments. - Analyzing Raman spectra of ancient carbon inks on papyrus. - The correlation of spectral change and date of writing. - The AIL date prediction model. - Testing the AIL prediction model. - The limits of the AIL prediction model. - The Gospel of Jesus' Wife and the Gospel of John. - Conclusion.
